items.followUp: Define ecosystem and describe how its biotic and abiotic components interact.

rubric.why: A population consists of organisms of one species living in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the definition; 1 mark if only the same-species or same-area idea is given.

rubric.why: A community is formed by populations of different species living and interacting in an area.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the definition including interaction; 1 mark if it mentions different populations in the same area but not interaction.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.followUp: State four differences between an organ and an organ system.

rubric.why: The presence or absence of a membrane-bound nucleus is a fundamental difference.
rubric.description: Compares the nucleus in the two cell types.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for correctly contrasting both types; 1 mark for a correct statement about only one type.

rubric.why: Eukaryotic cells contain membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotic cells do not.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and have 70S ribosomes, while eukaryotic cells are generally larger and have 80S ribosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct comparison, such as size or ribosomes.

rubric.why: Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular and not enclosed in a nucleus; eukaryotic DNA is organized into linear chromosomes in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in DNA or chromosome organization.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain them.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotic cells are generally larger and have 80S ribosomes.
Prokaryotic DNA is usually circular and lies in the nucleoid; eukaryotic DNA is organized into linear chromosomes in the nucleus.

items.followUp: Write any four characteristics of viruses.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts; this is a defining characteristic.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for this characteristic.

rubric.why: Enzymes increase the rate of biochemical reactions.
rubric.description: States that enzymes speed up reactions.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for this characteristic.

rubric.why: An enzyme is not used up during the reaction and can be used again.
rubric.description: States that enzymes remain unchanged or are reusable.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for this characteristic.

rubric.why: Enzymes show specificity and have other characteristic properties such as protein nature and optimum conditions.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for one correct additional characteristic.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up biochemical reactions.
They are not consumed in the reactions and can be reused.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
Enzymes are proteins and work best at an optimum temperature and pH.

items.followUp: Describe the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis and identify where they take place.

rubric.why: A photosystem is a light-absorbing pigment-protein complex in the thylakoid membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a pigment-protein light-harvesting complex in the thylakoid membrane.

rubric.why: In the Calvin cycle, carbon dioxide is fixed to RuBP and forms 3-PGA.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the fixation step and product; 1 mark for a partially correct account.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH provide energy and reducing power to convert 3-PGA into G3P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking ATP and NADPH with formation of G3P.

rubric.why: Some G3P is used to make sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP so the cycle can continue.
rubric.description: States the outcomes and regeneration step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sugar formation or RuBP regeneration.

modelAnswer: A photosystem is a light-absorbing complex of pigments and proteins in the thylakoid membrane.
The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.
Carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and is fixed by the enzyme RuBisCO, forming 3-PGA.
ATP and NADPH are used to reduce 3-PGA to G3P.
Some G3P is used to form sugars, while the rest regenerates RuBP using ATP, allowing the cycle to continue.

items.followUp: Define taxonomy and state what it helps biologists do.

rubric.why: Biogeography is the study of the geographical distribution of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for identifying the study of organisms' geographical distribution; 1 mark for a partial definition.

modelAnswer: Biogeography is the study of the geographical distribution of organisms, both living and extinct.

items.followUp: What are quantitative observations? Give one example.

rubric.why: Qualitative observations describe qualities rather than numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing them as non-numerical or descriptive observations.

rubric.why: A suitable example describes a quality without giving a measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid non-numerical example.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe the qualities or features of something without using numbers.
For example, a leaf is green.

rubric.why: A deduction is a conclusion or inference made from observations, often using prior knowledge.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining a deduction as a conclusion drawn from observations; 1 mark for mentioning only a conclusion or inference.

modelAnswer: Deductions are logical conclusions drawn from observations, often using prior knowledge.

Pea: Pisum sativum.
